key_insight: Efficient attention can lose important information when it routes queries using only average similarity. This paper proposes generalized second-order routing for multi-state linear attention to go beyond that mean-only view.
problem_solved: Standard self-attention scales quadratically with sequence length. Multi-state linear attention offers a more efficient alternative, but its mean-based routing can overlook differences in how a query aligns with keys within each segment.
method: Split a long context into segments and compress each segment into its own memory state.
Use generalized second-order routing to enrich how queries select and combine information from those states.
The supplied abstract is truncated; exact routing equations, implementation details, and experimental results are unavailable.
impact: The approach targets more informative memory routing for efficient long-context models. Its practical speed, memory, and accuracy benefits cannot be assessed from the supplied excerpt.
